metadata.topic: Gas Laws — Boyle's Law: Read Volume from P vs 1/V Graph
metadata.note: 3m: read volume at P=250kPa from the P vs 1/V graph. Graph is linear through origin; given point (1/V=0.030 cm⁻³, P=400kPa). Gradient = PV = 400/0.030 = 13333 kPa·cm³. At P=250kPa: 1/V = 250/13333 = 0.01875 cm⁻³ → V = 53.3 cm³. Q3c(iii) uses this as V₁ (already authored in Q3ciii file).

question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q3c(ii) — Boyle's Law: Determine Volume at P = 250 kPa
question.text:
The graph of pressure (p) versus inverse volume (1/V) is a straight line through the origin. The line passes through the point (1/V = 0.030 cm⁻³, p = 400 kPa).

(ii) Use the graph to determine the volume when the pressure is 250 kPa. (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Reading V at P = 250 kPa from the P vs 1/V graph:

The graph is linear through origin, so: P = k × (1/V) where k = PV = constant.

From the given point: k = 400 × (1/0.030) = 400/0.030 × cm³ → wait: k = P/(1/V) = P × V = 400 kPa × (1/0.030 cm⁻³) — no:

Since y = P and x = 1/V, gradient = P/(1/V) = P×V = k = 400/0.030 = 13 333 kPa cm³

At P = 250 kPa: 1/V = P/k = 250/13 333 = 0.01875 cm⁻³

V = 1/0.01875 = 53.3 cm³

steps.label:
Graph: P vs 1/V is linear through origin | Known point: (1/V = 0.030 cm⁻³, P = 400 kPa)
Gradient (= PV constant): k = P ÷ (1/V) = P × V
Determine V when P = 250 kPa. (3 marks)

fields.label: Gradient k = P × V = _____ kPa cm³
fields.diagnostic_hint: k = P/(1/V) = 400/0.030 = 13 333 kPa cm³ (from the given graph point)

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: From the graph, at 1/V = 0.030 cm⁻³, P = 400 kPa. Gradient = P ÷ (1/V) = 400 ÷ 0.030 = 13 333 kPa cm³. This equals PV = constant (Boyle's law).

fields.label: Volume V at P = 250 kPa = _____ cm³
fields.diagnostic_hint: V = 1/(1/V) = 1/0.01875 = 53.3 cm³. Accept 51–55 cm³ for graph-reading variation.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: From the graph: at P = 250 kPa, read off the 1/V value, then take the reciprocal to get V.
